content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xpath 1.0, 2.0, and 3.1 within XPath. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XPath 1.0, 2.0, and 3.1 matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about core differences, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XPath selects nodes and values from a data model. A location path is built from steps; predicates filter candidate nodes. Prefixes in a query must be bound by the host query context, even when the XML uses a different prefix for the same namespace URI.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Core differences; Node sets versus sequences; Data types and type-aware expressions; Maps and arrays in XPath 3.1; Processor and host-language compatibility. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: XPath 1.0, 2.0, and 3.1
content_blocks.expected_output: On a catalog containing products with numeric price child elements, this XPath selects the names of products whose price is greater than 10.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Start with a small expression, compare it with the expected set of nodes, and then add one predicate at a time. XPath 1.0 and XPath 2.0/3.1 differ in data model and expression features, so record the processor and supported version.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: XPath version support and namespace-prefix registration depend on the selected host application or query processor.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Record the exact processor and version: specification support is not universal, especially for XSD 1.1, XPath 2.0/3.1, XQuery, and XSLT 2.0/3.0.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Core differences”. Then add one boundary case involving “Node sets versus sequences”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
